newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint edges up vs dlr on mark's gains.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint edges up vs dlr on mark's gains.

text.p: Hungary's forint firmed against the dollar on Monday as the U.S currency weakened in the mark cross, dealers said.

"(The forint) followed the dollar/mark," said Gabor Jakab of BNP-Dresdner Bank, adding that the forint remained pinned to the National Bank of Hungary's resistance level (NBH bid) all day. "The forint is strong."
The Hungarian currency ended at 185.10/15 to the dollar, compared with 185.67/72 at the opening and 185.50/70 at midday.
Dealers said they did not see any factors to move the forint away the NBH bid in the near future.
"Privatisation is advancing, foreign currency loans are still relatively cheap and imports bills are unlikely to be as high this month as at the end of last month," Jakab said.
(The NBH's floating intervention band is 4.5 percent wide. The forint floats against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.)
